full_judgment: 9. In the facts and circumstances of the instant case, rule 17(1) as quoted hereinbefore is attracted. The words "the Courts may make an order that the appeal be dismissed" as used in rule 17(1) is very important. By the said words it meant that the Court may dismiss the appeal or may adjourn it to some other date or pass other order, but it certainly does not authorize the Court to consider an appeal in the absence of the appellants and decide it on merits. Therefore, the appellants having been defaulted to appear before the single Bench when the appeal was called on for hearing either it had to dismiss the appeal for default or to adjourn it or to pass any other order, but in no case it could allow the same on merits setting aside the judgment and decree of the appellate Court and restore those of the trial Court. The thing will be clearer if we consider rule 19 of Order XLI of the Code. The said rule has provided that where an appeal is dismissed under rule I I, sub-rule (2), or rule 15A or rule 17 or rule 18 the appellant may apply to the appellate Court for re-admission of the appeal; and, where it is proved that the appellant was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the appeal was called for hearing or from depositing the sum so required, the Court shall re-admit the appeal on such terms as to costs or otherwise as it thinks fit. It is Sery pertinent to note that by way of amendment sub-rule (2) was inserted to rule 19 of Order XLI of the Code making the provisions of section 5 of the Limitation Act, '1908 applicable in respect of an application for re-admission of an appeal. In this regard, it is also necessary to state that a new rule being 19A was inserted in Order XLI of the Code by Act VIII of 2006 making provision for direct re-admission of appeal notwithstanding anything contained in rule 19 or any other law if an application supported by affidavit, praying for such re-admission is made to the Court within thirty days Of the date on which the appeal is dismissed for default. Thus, from the above provisions of the Code it appears to us that the concept of ex-parte disposal of an appeal on merits in either way in the absence of the appellant has not been conceived of in the Code. Had the concept of disposal of an appeal on merits in the absence of the appellant was conceived of the provision of re-admission of an appeal dismissed for default would not have been made.
